script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour. During the examination, you will hear several recordings. You will have time to read the instructions and the questions. You will also have time to check your work.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part A. Task 1. You are at the reception desk for the SlashFest 2026 Youth Career Summit. You will hear a conversation between a staff member and a delegate. Complete the registration form below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Good morning! Welcome to SlashFest 2026. We are expecting a huge crowd today—nearly one thousand young professionals. How can I help you with your registration today?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Hello! I'm here to pick up my badge. My name is Marcus Chui. I'm a Graphic Designer and Coffee Roaster. I believe I'm registered under the Young Professional category.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Let me see... Marcus Chui... Ah, yes, here it is. Your mobile is 9122 3847 and your email is m.chui@creativelab.hk. Your Badge ID is SF-2026-MC.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: That's correct. And my sponsorship tier?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: You're on the Silver tier. Your sponsorship amount is $5,500. Your booth location is B12. I also see you're affiliated with the Freelance Union HK.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Yes, Freelance Union HK. And I'm attending the 'Monetizing Passion' workshop this afternoon.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Monetizing Passion. Got it. You're all set, Marcus. Enjoy SlashFest!

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. You will hear a keynote presentation by Dr. Elena Vong on 'The Rise of the Slashie'. Listen to the presentation and complete the notes below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Dr Vong
script.text: Good morning, everyone. I'm Dr. Elena Vong. Our recent Youth Career Index shows a staggering 65% adoption rate for the 'Slashie' lifestyle among Gen Z in Hong Kong. We call this the Portfolio Career—a deliberate blending of diverse professional roles.

script.speaker: Dr Vong
script.text: Traditional job security has seen a 40% loss in the last five years, but we see an 85% increase in life satisfaction among successful slashies. This is 'Work-Life Integration'—blending career goals with personal identity. However, high property prices remain the main barrier. Currently, 55% of slashies work remotely.

script.speaker: Dr Vong
script.text: The government has introduced a Digital Nomad Visa. The target age demographic for the new startup fund is 18 to 35. We are also proposing the Freelance Fairness Act, specifically Article 18C, which mandates a 30-day payment cycle. Thank you.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. You will hear a panel of three experts discussing 'Slashie Sustainability'. Listen to the discussion and tick the correct boxes in the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome to our panel. Joining us are Cecilia, Mr. Cheng, and Sam. Cecilia, tell us about your dual roles.

script.speaker: Cecilia
script.text: I'm a Graphic Designer and Yoga Instructor. The biggest hurdle is the Self-Employed Person or SEP status. The mandatory MPF contribution rate is 5% of net income. Health insurance premiums for independents have risen 12% this year, which is why I use GigGuard HK.

script.speaker: Mr Cheng
script.text: As an employer, I love hiring slashies. It gives us access to diverse skillsets without full-time overhead.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: My concern is tax complexity. Young slashies face complex reporting for multiple income streams. The good news is the Slashie Startup Grant offers 1.2 million dollars. The deadline is July 31.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: What are the qualifying criteria?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: You need a minimum of 15 hours per week and max income for tax exemption is $120,000.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Thank you to our moderator, Dr. Felix Ho.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. You will hear three stakeholders discussing the 'Freelance Fairness Act'. Listen to their conversation and complete the matrix below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Today we're joined by a Union Representative, a Platform CEO, and a Freelancer. Union Rep, what's your priority?

script.speaker: Union Rep
script.text: Enforceable payment timelines. Currently, 38% of invoices in Hong Kong's gig economy are paid late. Article 18C will fix this.

script.speaker: CEO
script.text: I support fairness, but my concern is liability for individual worker safety. And worker misclassification is a grey area.

script.speaker: Freelancer
script.text: We need protection against ghosting clients. The Labor Bureau Youth Division should oversee this. Stakeholder support is at 92%.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: What about the grant?

script.speaker: Union Rep
script.text: The Slashie Startup Grant offers 1.2 million dollars. The public hearing is on September 14. Feedback can be sent to fairness@labor.gov.hk.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of Part A. You now have five minutes to study the Part B Question-Answer Book and the Data File. (300-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Integrated Skills Recording. You will now hear a briefing from the CEO of Creative Lab, Janice Wong, to the Project Manager regarding the upcoming tasks. Listen carefully and take notes as you will need this information to complete the tasks in Part B.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Good morning. I'm glad we're finally getting started on these tasks. We have a lot to do before the Q4 rollout. When you write that letter to the Platform CEO for Task 8, please don't just repeat the brochure points. Emphasise that we aren't just creating 'gig' jobs for delivery riders. Mention that we are specifically looking to hire people with 'project management skills' and 'client relations experience' to bridge the gap between freelance platforms and corporate clients. That's a key detail not in the Data File yet.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Moving on to the internal memo for Task 9—don't just list the budget gap. Propose a specific 'Freelance Fairness Week' in October to fix the publicity issue. We need to get local business podcasts involved to build trust. And for the public social media post in Task 10, make sure to use a friendly, non-corporate tone. Use the phrase 'Passion with Paycheck' and make it sound like a friend talking to a friend.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: One last thing—I just heard from the Labor Bureau. They are very insistent that we describe our payment protection system as 'Bank Grade'. That's the specific term they want us to use in our responses to citizens like Mr. David Lee. 'Bank Grade'. Got it? Good. I expect those drafts on my desk by the end of the day. Good luck.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of the Integrated Skills recording. You now have 1 hour and 10 minutes to complete your tasks. Stop writing when you hear the signal at the end of the examination.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (4200-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Stop writing now. The examination is over. Please stay in your seats until your scripts have been collected.

data_file.title: Minutes of the SlashFest 2026 Steering Committee Meeting
data_file.content:
Date: June 10, 2026
Location: Conference Room B, Gov HQ

Attendees: Mr. K.W. Ho (Labor Bureau), Ms. Sarah Jenkins (Public Relations), Dr. Simon Lee (Economics Consultant).

Main Points:
1. Mr. Ho noted that public trust in the gig economy is currently low (approx 32% approval). We need to address freelancers' fear of 'income instability'.
2. Ms. Jenkins suggested a 'Passion with Paycheck' campaign. The goal is to highlight how the Slashie economy creates new categories of jobs (e.g., Platform Coordinators, Portfolio Career Coaches).
3. Action Item: Draft a persuasive letter to the Platform CEOs to calm nerves before the Q4 2026 rollout.
4. Note: Avoid technical jargon. Use the 'Future of Work' slogan.

data_file.title: SlashFest 2026: Official Program Highlights
data_file.content:
A Vision for the Future:
- Total Investment: $800 Million HKD.
- Key Pillar: Freelance Fairness Act (Article 18C already drafted).
- Upcoming: Labor Bureau Youth Division oversight office to open by November.

Why Slashies?
Flexibility is not just about hours; it's about designing a career that fits your life. Our pilot co-working hubs have already supported 2,000 slashies in the first quarter.

data_file.title: Email from a Concerned Citizen (Mr. David Lee)
data_file.content:
To: Labor Bureau Feedback
Subject: Payment Concerns regarding Freelance Platforms

I am a freelance web developer and I am extremely uncomfortable with the 60-day payment delays on some platforms. Who is protecting our income? Is there enforcement? I heard rumours that GigGuard HK is rejecting claims. Please clarify immediately or I will organise a freelancer strike.

data_file.title: Editorial: The Gig Economy and the $1.2M Question
data_file.content:
South China Morning Post - June 15, 2026

While the government brags about 'Slashie' status, thousands of young freelancers are being left behind. Dr. Vong's proposal for a $1.2M grant is a good start, but it won't fix the 38% unpaid invoice rate which is a barrier for many. We need a 'Freelance Safety Net' that includes both funding and legal protection.

data_file.title: Urgent Note from CEO Janice Wong (Post-it Note)
data_file.content:
To: Project Manager

Just saw David Lee's email (Doc 3). We MUST reply to him. Be firm but polite. Explain that payment data is ENCRYPTED and never shared. Also, mention the Labor Bureau Youth Division is overseeing this. We can't afford a strike right now. Also, for the internal memo (Task 9), make sure you mention we are hiring 120 'Platform Liaisons' to show we are creating jobs!

data_file.title: Table 1: SlashFest Budget vs. Actual Spending (Q1 2026)
data_file.content:
Category | Budgeted | Actual | Status
--------------------------------------------
Hardware | $200M | $220M | Over-budget
Consultancy | $80M | $70M | Under-budget
Publicity | $60M | $25M | Critical Gap
Staffing | $150M | $140M | On track

Note: The 'Publicity' gap is why the public is currently so skeptical. We need to increase podcast presence immediately.

data_file.title: Viral Post from 'HK Freelancers United'
data_file.content:
Shared 4,200 times:
'THEY ARE EXPLOITING US! The new Freelance Fairness Act is too weak. They talk about "flexibility" but we know it means "precarity." Stand with us on July 1st! #NoToGhostClients #ProtectOurPay'

data_file.title: Internal Memo: Staffing Update
data_file.content:
Internal Use Only
Subject: New Role Creation - Platform Liaisons

To counter the negative PR, we are announcing the creation of 120 'Platform Liaison' roles. These staff will be deployed to co-working hubs to teach 'Digital Client Management'. This proves our Slashie policy creates jobs for humans too!

data_file.title: Tech News Daily: GigGuard HK Partnership
data_file.content: GigGuard HK has officially signed a deal to provide discounted health and equipment insurance to all freelancers registered under the Freelance Union HK. This move aims to protect the most vulnerable from the recent surge in unpaid invoice disputes.

data_file.title: Draft Section: Payment Protection Laws
data_file.content: Clause 5.2: All freelance platform payments must be processed within 30 days. Late fees under Article 18C apply after day 31. The Labor Bureau Youth Division will maintain a public blacklist of repeat offenders.
